rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so all design dimensions carry maximum uncertainty. The most informative first step is to establish the simplest possible performance baseline: RNA-only, single-profile, PCA (2000 components). This tells us (1) whether the task is tractable with minimal modeling, (2) what performance floor to compare against when adding complexity (better encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image modality, fusion), and (3) whether the RNA signal alone is sufficient or whether multimodal integration is necessary. Every subsequent experiment can be interpreted as a delta over this reference, making it the highest-information-per-experiment choice under a tight budget. It is also computationally inexpensive, reducing the risk of a costly failure on the first run.

Evidence: Only one experiment (config_001, rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000) has been completed, yielding a low baseline of ~48.5% accuracy. This tells us little about whether the image modality carries any useful signal for this task. Uncertainty: The most consequential architectural question is whether image features contribute meaningfully at all—if they do not, ~28 multimodal/image-only configurations can be eliminated from consideration. What this tests: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest possible probe of image-modality signal, using a standard, well-established backbone (ResNet-50) and matching the singleprofile setting of the RNA baseline for a fair unimodal comparison. Why it is the best next experiment: Under a tight budget, resolving the binary question 'does image modality help?' has the highest information value because it branches the entire remaining search space. If image accuracy is comparable to or below the RNA baseline, I can focus subsequent experiments on RNA encoder and profile improvements. If it is substantially higher, I can prioritize multimodal fusion strategies. No other single experiment would reduce uncertainty about this many downstream decisions.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA-2000 and single profile (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, far outperforming image-only ResNet50 (config_010, 20.8%), establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We have no data on whether multiprofile aggregation improves the RNA signal, and this is a foundational design axis that affects all downstream multimodal experiments. What this tests: config_002 is a minimal, controlled extension of config_001—same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), same modality—adding only multiprofile with avgpool aggregation. This gives a clean A/B comparison of single vs. multi profile for the dominant modality. Why it is the best next experiment: (1) RNA is the performance driver, so improving it has the highest expected impact; (2) the result directly informs whether the entire multiprofile branch (configs 003, 005–009, 018–051) is worth pursuing, reducing uncertainty across ~40 remaining configurations; (3) the minimal change from config_001 makes the comparison interpretable without confounding variables; (4) under a tight budget, resolving this binary question (does multiprofile help?) is more informative than jumping to a new encoder or fusion strategy whose interpretation would be muddied by the unknown profile effect.

Evidence: Multi-profile RNA with PCA_n2000 + avgpool (config_002, acc 0.591) substantially outperforms single-profile (config_001, acc 0.485), confirming that profile aggregation is a high-impact design choice. Image-only (config_010, acc 0.208) is very weak, so the RNA pathway is the primary signal source and must be optimized before multimodal fusion is informative. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether transformer aggregation outperforms simple avgpool for combining multiple profiles—this is the next most consequential architectural decision after establishing that multi-profile helps. This experiment (config_003) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding everything else at the best-known RNA settings (PCA_n2000, multi-profile), making it a clean, minimal test of one variable. It is the best use of the next budget slot because it directly extends the strongest configuration, reduces uncertainty on a design axis that will propagate into all multimodal experiments, and avoids the confound of simultaneously changing encoder, profile setting, and fusion strategy.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool; acc 0.591), showing that multiprofile + avgpool is a strong RNA setup. However, we have only tested one RNA encoder (PCA) across all experiments, leaving the encoder choice as a major unexplored design axis. Question: Does a learned single-cell encoder (scvi_n200) outperform linear PCA in the best-performing multiprofile+avgpool configuration? This directly tests whether the encoder captures non-linear biological structure that PCA misses. Why this is the best next experiment: The RNA encoder is a foundational design decision that will propagate into all multimodal experiments. Resolving whether scvi or PCA is superior here (with a clean single-variable change from config_002) reduces uncertainty efficiently before committing budget to the larger multimodal grid. If scvi matches or beats PCA, it reshapes the multimodal search; if it underperforms, PCA is confirmed as sufficient and we can pivot to multimodal fusion with confidence.

Evidence so far shows RNA (scvi_n200, multi, avgpool) is the strongest modality at 0.650 acc, while image-only (ResNet50) is very weak at 0.208. The critical open question is whether the image modality contributes complementary signal when fused with the best RNA configuration, or whether it is purely noise that degrades performance. Config_030 (multimodal, multi, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) directly tests this by pairing the strongest RNA setup with the weakest image encoder under the simplest fusion (concat). If accuracy exceeds 0.650, multimodal fusion is worth further exploration (ViT, weighted fusion); if it falls below, the image branch is not useful and remaining budget should focus on RNA encoder/aggregation refinements. This single experiment resolves the highest-uncertainty design decision—whether to invest in multimodal or unimodal strategies—making it the most budget-efficient next step.

Evidence: RNA encoder choice is the strongest lever so far—pca_n2000 (config_002, 0.591) vs scvi_n200 (config_005, 0.650) with identical multiprofile/avgpool setup shows a ~6-point gain. scgpt is completely untested. Question: config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is a clean single-variable A/B against config_005, isolating whether scgpt matches, exceeds, or underperforms scvi_n200. Why best next: the RNA encoder is the most fundamental design axis and propagates into every multimodal configuration; resolving this uncertainty before further multimodal/fusion experiments avoids wasting budget on suboptimal encoder choices. If scgpt is clearly superior, all subsequent multimodal tests should use it; if similar or worse, we can confidently commit to scvi_n200 and pivot to fusion-method or image-encoder questions.

Evidence: The current best is config_005 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650. The only multimodal test (config_030: scvi_n200 + resnet50, avgpool, concat) scored 0.632, slightly *worse* than RNA-only, suggesting the weak resnet50 image encoder (image-only acc=0.208) adds noise. Key uncertainty: is the image modality fundamentally uninformative, or was resnet50 simply too weak to contribute useful signal? This experiment (config_036) pairs the best-validated RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) with the strongest available image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) using the same concat fusion. It directly tests whether a stronger visual encoder can make multimodal fusion competitive with or exceed the RNA-only baseline. If it succeeds, it opens a promising multimodal direction; if it fails, we can confidently abandon multimodal and focus remaining budget on RNA-only refinements. This is the highest-information experiment available because it resolves the single most consequential design question (is multimodal worth pursuing?) with one test, rather than incrementally tuning a direction that already appears suboptimal.

Evidence: config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieved the best validation accuracy (0.715) and F1 (0.687), substantially outperforming both RNA-only (0.650) and the resnet50-based multimodal (0.632). This establishes that the combination of scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + avgpool is the strongest design. Uncertainty: The only untested dimension within this top-performing configuration is the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted). Question tested: Does weighted fusion improve over simple concatenation when combining the scvi_n200 RNA embedding with the imagenet_vit_l image embedding? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a minimal, single-variable change from the current best configuration, so any performance delta is cleanly attributable to the fusion method. If weighted fusion helps, we immediately identify an even better configuration; if not, we confirm concat is optimal and can redirect exploration. Under a limited budget, exploiting the strongest direction with the smallest remaining uncertainty is the most efficient use of the next experiment.

The best result so far is config_036 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 acc. In RNA-only experiments, avgpool consistently outperformed transformer aggregation (pca: 0.591 vs 0.519; scvi: 0.650 vs untested), but that evidence comes from weaker encoder combinations. The key remaining uncertainty for the top-performing multimodal setup is whether transformer aggregation could exploit cross-profile interactions more effectively when paired with the strong ViT image features. config_038 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer (keeping concat fusion, which slightly beat weighted), directly testing this interaction. If transformer improves performance, it opens a new optimization axis; if it confirms avgpool superiority, we can confidently lock in the aggregation choice and focus remaining budget on other design dimensions. This is the highest-information experiment because it resolves the last untested design variable in the strongest configuration family.
